nodes.label: Collision Avoidance Positioning
nodes.rationale: Multi-session shared-checkout collision avoidance was selected as the core open-source differentiation after the market audit.

nodes.label: Hook Inheritance Interoperability
nodes.rationale: Other orchestrators reuse the user's Claude Code configuration, so Orchestra can observe their spawned agents without bespoke integrations, provided its hooks fail soft.

nodes.label: Coordination Gap
nodes.rationale: Competitors isolate or spawn agents but do not provide cross-workspace path claims, collision warnings, or agent-to-agent communication.

nodes.label: Vibe Kanban SQLite Migration
nodes.rationale: The local tasks schema maps almost one-to-one to Orchestra cards, making an import command a small, high-leverage adoption wedge for the orphaned community.

nodes.label: Overlap Detection
nodes.rationale: Glob-aware overlap detection warns agents about intersecting active scopes while remaining advisory.

nodes.label: CLI and Hook Runner
nodes.rationale: Thin commands and fail-soft hook subcommands expose one API to agents, humans, and Claude Code lifecycle events without putting daemon logic in hooks.

nodes.label: Packaging CI and Manual Launch Gate
nodes.rationale: Automated testing and tagged publishing prepare the package, while repository creation, publishing, and launch posts remain behind explicit user authorization.
nodes.norm_label: packaging ci and manual launch gate

nodes.label: Single Daemon Three Clients
nodes.rationale: A single local Fastify and SQLite writer gives hooks, CLI sessions, and the web UI one consistent coordination state while avoiding multi-writer concurrency problems.

nodes.label: Advisory Overlap Check
nodes.rationale: Path-prefix and glob intersections should surface warnings before agents collide but should never act as a lock.

nodes.label: Fail Soft Adoption
nodes.rationale: One-command, offline, account-free adoption only works if short-lived hooks always exit successfully and never break a Claude session when the daemon is unavailable.

nodes.label: Zero Workflow Change
nodes.rationale: Auto-registering sessions users already run is the differentiated asset because it avoids forcing an orchestrator-owned workflow.

nodes.label: Shared Checkout Collision Avoidance
nodes.rationale: A pragmatic segment avoids worktree friction by opening multiple terminals in one checkout, so the launch story centers on keeping those disjoint tasks safe.

nodes.label: Edit Time and Git State Guards
nodes.rationale: Pulse warnings may arrive after a collision, and branch-mutating commands can silently disrupt every session, so checks should run before writes and shared-git mutations.
nodes.norm_label: edit time and git state guards

nodes.label: Worktree Conflict Forecasting
nodes.rationale: Worktrees isolate execution but defer overlapping changes until merge, making cross-worktree diff overlap a later expansion opportunity.

nodes.label: Cross Tool Coordination Positioning
nodes.rationale: The durable moat is ambient hook-based coordination and conflict forecasting across independently run tools, not the commoditized kanban surface.

nodes.label: UI Error Visibility
nodes.rationale: A reconnecting banner and write-error toasts turn silent failures and misleading empty states into actionable feedback.

nodes.label: Cost and Transcript Persistence
nodes.rationale: Persisted transcripts and complete token or cost accounting would make hired-agent activity auditable across restarts.

nodes.label: Multiplexed SSE
nodes.rationale: A single debounced stream avoids browser connection exhaustion and repeated all-board refetches.

nodes.label: Attach Dont Spawn
nodes.rationale: Orchestra should coordinate independently run sessions rather than own their workspaces, making it complementary to agent spawners and native teams.

nodes.label: Oversight Without Takeover
nodes.rationale: The product should sit between vanilla parallel sessions and heavily autonomous orchestration that demands constant steering.

nodes.label: Buyer Based Open Core
nodes.rationale: Keep individual development local and free while reserving manager or team oversight for paid offerings because individual kanban pricing failed.

nodes.label: Review Capacity Hero
nodes.rationale: Review triage, blast-radius signals, and cross-agent change queues directly address the bottleneck practitioners consistently report.

nodes.label: Native Absorption and Migration
nodes.rationale: Build the cross-session wedge while native teams remain session-scoped, and use the compatible Vibe Kanban database as an immediate migration path.

nodes.label: Optimistic Updates
nodes.rationale: Applying actions immediately and reconciling on refresh removes the lag caused by waiting for a write plus a full snapshot round trip.

nodes.label: Git Working Branch and Remote Pairing
nodes.norm_label: git working branch and remote pairing

nodes.label: Seven Day Dogfood Gate
nodes.rationale: The promised seven-day real-world usage window cannot honestly be marked complete before 2026-07-24.

nodes.label: Authentic Demo Gate
nodes.rationale: Launch footage must capture the real three-terminal and web UI workflow rather than substitute a mock.

nodes.label: Plugin Marketplace Dependency
nodes.rationale: Bundled hooks must be retested after the npm package exists because marketplace installation depends on that package.

nodes.label: Verified Delivery Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Independent verification plus a serialized, test-gated auto-ship queue makes delivery status trustworthy rather than self-reported.

nodes.label: Local First Privacy
nodes.rationale: Binding to loopback, storing state locally, and sending no project data to an Orchestra service keep coordination private.

nodes.label: Advisory Path Claims
nodes.rationale: Agents claim paths and receive overlap warnings to reduce duplicate work and same-file edits without imposing locks.

nodes.label: Local First MIT
nodes.rationale: A loopback daemon, local SQLite, no hosted account, and an MIT license make the tool inspectable and self-contained.

nodes.label: Test and Package Quality Gate
nodes.rationale: Install, type-check, unit-test, run E2E, build, and dry-run packaging so defects are caught before publication.

nodes.label: Version-Tag npm Publication
nodes.rationale: Publish publicly with provenance only after tests pass and only from version tags.

nodes.label: Multi-Session Collision Avoidance
nodes.rationale: Positioned as the core open-source differentiation after a market audit found a persistent cross-session coordination gap.

nodes.label: Token-Diet Milestone 2
nodes.rationale: Reduce recurring session overhead; the recorded result was a 58.6 percent reduction from 1120 to 464 tokens per session.

nodes.label: Web UI Audit
nodes.rationale: Surface reliability, refetching, EventSource, confirmation, accessibility, and responsive-design gaps.

nodes.label: Cross-Session Coordination and Review Triage
nodes.rationale: Identified as a defensible niche because competitors lack cross-session enrollment and review capacity, rather than merge conflicts, is the bottleneck.

nodes.label: Terminal Parity Invariant
nodes.rationale: Managed agents must not hide or weaken the raw PTY, output, signal, and command-history capabilities of a real terminal.

nodes.label: Provider-Neutral Agent Kernel
nodes.rationale: Core state and server/UI contracts use provider-neutral types so Claude, Codex, shell, and future drivers can share one operating model.

nodes.label: Durable Reconstructable State
nodes.rationale: Durable records are authoritative and in-memory projections are disposable caches, enabling restart recovery and auditability.

nodes.label: Operator and Agent Credential Boundary
nodes.rationale: Agents may report and verify, but only the server-derived operator principal may accept, reject, override, approve, send back, or complete managed work.

nodes.label: Claims and Evidence Separation
nodes.rationale: Agent statements remain useful claims but never become proof without independently observed evidence.

nodes.label: Immutable Delivery Revision Lineage
nodes.rationale: Rejected attempts stay auditable and revisions become linked child reports instead of rewriting prior history.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Compatibility Gate
nodes.rationale: When legacy and canonical execution identities are ambiguous, select the latest managed job and block completion instead of reusing stale acceptance.

nodes.label: Subscription-First Provider Strategy
nodes.rationale: Personal subscriptions through native terminal CLIs are primary; usage-priced provider APIs are explicit secondary modes and never silent fallbacks.

nodes.label: Canonical, Compatibility, Legacy, and Infrastructure Classification
nodes.norm_label: canonical, compatibility, legacy, and infrastructure classification

nodes.label: Server Composition Boundary
nodes.rationale: The composition layer owns lifecycle, authentication, dependency injection, and route registration while excluding canonical transitions, service construction, persistence, and validation.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Compatibility Migration
nodes.rationale: The physical handoff validates identity and lifecycle, quarantines ambiguous rows, aborts transactionally on failure, and does not automatically demote canonical writes.

nodes.label: Surface Drift-Check Contract
nodes.rationale: Exact comparison makes newly added or removed tables, routes, commands, event kinds, and UI markers require deliberate classification and human review.

nodes.label: Retained Tarball Verification
nodes.rationale: A tester must verify the owner-supplied SHA-256 and source commit because a local archive is distribution, not provenance or a public release.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Onboarding Plan
nodes.rationale: Onboarding rederives its plan from safe identifiers and an immutable manifest, rejects apply on any blocker, and does not trust client-returned advanced fields.

nodes.label: Explicit Provider API Mode
nodes.rationale: Provider API mode requires a literal usage-priced acknowledgement and cannot be silently selected when subscription readiness fails.

nodes.label: Preserve State on Uninstall
nodes.rationale: Package and hook removal does not authorize deleting ORCHESTRA_HOME, worktrees, projects, or the retained artifact.

nodes.label: Safe Backup and Restore Protocol
nodes.rationale: Hooks must be quiesced, the recorded daemon process must exit, and health must remain offline before moving SQLite state with its WAL companions.

nodes.label: Allowlisted Diagnostics Bundle
nodes.rationale: Diagnostics are closed-schema, bounded, redacted, locally reviewed, and written owner-only; they are not an arbitrary archive or automatically safe to share.

nodes.label: Functional Beta, Not Safe Remote Beta
nodes.rationale: Observed tunnel exposure, reusable bearer pairing, broad reads, and direct delivery into tool-capable agents leave critical gaps despite existing controls.
nodes.norm_label: functional beta, not safe remote beta

nodes.label: Remote Request Default-Deny Policy
nodes.rationale: Every remote route must explicitly declare scope, resource, data class, field, cache, step-up, attribution, and abuse behavior before DeviceSession access is allowed.

nodes.label: Offline Read-Only Semantics
nodes.rationale: Authenticated API data stays network-only, mutations are never queued, and device caches are purged on logout, revocation, credential failure, or worker upgrade.

nodes.label: No-Tool Remote Message Path
nodes.rationale: Remote text is untrusted provenance and must not launder low-scope message authority into a live tool-capable agent without agent-control policy and step-up.
